summary: Aloft Sensing (Ann Arbor, Michigan) builds compact software-defined radar payloads for uncrewed vehicles, with a stated focus on stratospheric platforms (long-endurance aircraft, airships and balloons). NASA describes its HALE InSAR instrument as weighing less than 15 pounds (seven kilograms), using fewer than 300 watts, and locating itself from its own radar signals without GPS.
oneLiner: Compact software-defined radar payloads for uncrewed vehicles, with a focus on stratospheric platforms
thesis: A radar NASA puts at seven kilograms that positions itself without GPS fits long-endurance stratospheric surveillance. Task orders funded by the Air Force Research Laboratory through NASA Ames pay for demonstrations on the BAE PHASA-35 and Aerostar Thunderhead balloon.
stage: No venture round was found: EDGAR searches return no match and no page opened names an investor. USAspending lists eight contracts starting between January 2022 and September 2025 totalling $5,806,113.94, plus three NASA grants totalling $8,763,972. The SAM record (mirrored) gives a start date of 5 November 2019. The FCC granted three special temporary authorities for radar operation at 55 to 75 kft from 8 to 30 September 2026.

team.name: Lauren Wye
team.background: CEO and principal investigator for HALE InSAR per NASA. NASA says she was principal investigator of the CIRES CubeSat radar and led its development at SRI International.

team.name: Patrick Rennich
team.background: Radar contact in the August 2026 FCC exhibits. An April 2019 SRI International press release calls him principal research engineer, Signals and Space Technology Laboratory.

team.name: Brian Pollard
team.background: Chief Engineer and co-investigator for HALE InSAR per NASA's August 2025 article. No source opened states his prior employer.

questions: Per USAspending, AFRL funds the four NASA Ames task orders. Who is the sponsor inside AFRL, and is there a path to a production or programme-of-record buy?
What happened on the September 2026 stratospheric flight covered by the three FCC authorities: which platform, how long aloft, and did SAR, InSAR and MTI perform to specification?
The August 2026 FCC exhibits show a custom Aloft transceiver with an EMAG Technologies antenna. What does Aloft own in the hardware stack, and at what unit cost?
The SAM record gives a November 2019 start and USAspending awards begin in January 2022. Is the company seeking outside capital, and what would it be used for?
risks: All funding found is federal (about $14.6M). No non-government customer appears in any source, and the 2026 FCC exhibits say the imagery and data will not be sold commercially.
The radar depends on stratospheric platforms built by others (BAE's PHASA-35, Aerostar's Thunderhead balloon, airships), so demand is tied to third-party HALE programmes reaching operational use.
Small team (LinkedIn lists 2 to 10 employees) and no equity round found since 2019. It may not want venture capital or may be run as a contract R&D business.
unverified: A search summary attributes an Andreessen Horowitz seed and Series A to Aloft Sensing. No page opened supports it, and it most likely refers to a different Aloft.
NASA says the instrument was validated aboard an airship at 65,000 feet and on small stratospheric balloons, but gives no dates, platform names or results. Not independently confirmed.
The company claims micron-level localization and picosecond timing on its site and LinkedIn page. No independent test result was found.

sources.title: SEC EDGAR full-text search, no hits

announcement.what: The company's own blog announced an Air Force Phase I SBIR award, and no launch or funding-round announcement was found.
